explanation: Retrospective, context-free piece-identity lookup: at every position after the first the pole's strength is a fixed graded value of the current tokenizer piece alone (1.461 on ' Socialist' in three unrelated sentences, 1.413 on 'é', 1.272 on ' out', 1.143 on ' own', 1.124 on ' un', 1.075 on ' Cochrane', max 1.537 on 'аш'; token identity explains 100% of the scan's variance, position 2%, integrated gradients put all of each peak on that piece and none on an earlier one, and zero-ablating the pole moves next-token KL by only 0.0012 and is not flagged lookahead), so label a peak ACTIVE iff the text contains one of the 3,664 pieces of its firing set (7.3% of the 50,304-piece vocabulary at the 0.25-of-max line of 0.384; 7,212 pieces sit above 0.25 absolute and 104 above 1.0) and INACTIVE iff every piece of the text is outside it. That set is a fixed idiosyncratic list that no language, script, case, part-of-speech, frequency or morphology rule describes -- it fires on 'аш' 1.54, ' unse' 1.50, ' quel' 1.47, ' Socialist' 1.46, 'é' 1.41, ' Le' 1.41, ' pestic' 1.39, 'cig' 1.33, ' out' 1.27, ' du' 1.18, ' own' 1.14, ' un' 1.12, 'å' 0.70, 'ü' 0.87, 'λο' 0.90, 'メ' 0.89 and even ' her' 0.41 while its neighbours ' the' -0.01, ' in' -0.02, ' on' -0.13, ' one' -0.10, ' up' -0.12, 'ž' -0.05, 'ж' -0.04, 'ψ' -0.10, 'ç' 0.12, 'ø' 0.08, 'ğ' 0.10 and 'ζ' 0.12 stay silent and ' Socialist' fires where lowercase ' socialist' 0.26 does not (Tamil pieces are 0.3% active against Arabic 19%, so language and script do not decide it either); it is empty on digits (0.2% of digit-bearing pieces clear the line), on whitespace, punctuation, brackets, operators and numbers (0 of 7,642 scanned occurrences active) and on English prose built from core vocabulary (only 3.4% of English-only words clear the line; eight such sentences I measured peak at -0.001 to 0.17), so hard negatives must be core-vocabulary English sentences -- French, German, Greek, Arabic, Ukrainian and Korean sentences peak at 0.48-1.16 -- and must avoid the ordinary English pieces that do fire (' bowling' 0.79, ' ware' 0.80, ' elect' 0.80, ' foot' 0.73, ' ball' 0.65, ' heard' 0.62, ' fair' 0.59, ' game' 0.52, ' off' 0.55, ' down' 0.60, ' hired' 0.37), while a piece placed at the very first position of a sequence can read differently (' Socialist' 0.03 alone at position 0 versus 1.46 after any earlier token).
